Green water means algae, usually from low chlorine or weak filtration. 1) Brush walls and floor. 2) Shock with chlorine granular. 3) Add algaecide. 4) Run the filter 24 hours and backwash. 5) Keep chlorine at 1 to 3 ppm after. Want the chlorine dose for your pool size?
quickReplies: How much chlorine do I need?

responses: Cloudy water is usually caused by poor filtration, high pH or low chlorine. Check pH (7.2 to 7.6) and chlorine, run the filter longer and backwash it. If the sand is more than 5 years old, it may need replacing.

Keep free chlorine at 1 to 3 ppm. With SDIC granular, about 1.8 g per m3 raises chlorine by 1 ppm. Tell me your pool size (for example 8 x 4 x 1.5) and I'll calculate the starting dose. Always follow the product label.

Keep pool pH between 7.2 and 7.6. High pH makes chlorine weak and water cloudy; low pH irritates eyes and corrodes equipment. Test 2 to 3 times a week with a test kit and adjust with pH minus or pH plus.
Replace the UV lamp every 12 months, even if it still lights up, because UV strength drops with time. Clean the quartz sleeve at the same time. We stock replacement lamps.
Let's size it! Tell me your pool's length, width and average depth in meters (for example: 8 x 4 x 1.5), or the total volume in m3. For a round pool, give the diameter and depth.
